annotation.title_clean: Searches and seizure using a drone (F.S. 934.50, Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act)
annotation.title_en: Searches and seizure using a drone (F.S. 934.50, Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act)
annotation.venue: Online Sunshine, Florida Legislature (The 2026 Florida Statutes)
annotation.summary_en: Florida statute 934.50, the Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act, restricts drone use by law enforcement and others for surveillance. It sets warrant and emergency exceptions, civil remedies, criminal penalties and evidence exclusion. It also requires government agencies to use approved drone manufacturers for security and creates drone grant programs.
key_provisions_or_claims: Law enforcement may not use drones to gather evidence except under listed exceptions such as a warrant or imminent danger.
Prohibits drone imaging of private property with surveillance intent, violating reasonable privacy expectation, without written consent.
Civil damages, injunctions and attorney fees; misdemeanor and felony penalties for individuals; evidence obtained unlawfully is inadmissible.
Governmental agencies may only use drones from manufacturers approved by the Department of Management Services, with minimum security rules.
Creates drone grant programs for first responders to replace non-compliant drones, with cybersecurity analysis by the Florida Center for Cybersecurity.
